implementation_notes: Django's template language provides both halves of the pattern: {% extends "base.html" %} with {% block %} sections is the layout mechanism ({{ block.super }} for the parent's content) and {% include "_product_row.html" %} is the fragment insert - pass explicit values with {% include ... with product=p only %} so the fragment does not depend on ambient context, and use "ignore missing" only when absence is genuinely acceptable. Jinja2 (Flask) has the same shape (include/extends, without context, import for macros when a fragment needs an interface). The engines parse and cache templates per loader, so include lookup cost is directory resolution plus rendering.
pitfalls: {% include %} without only shares the whole context, so fragments depend on ambient variables and silently render nothing (or wrong data) when reused - the common cause of "works on one page only" fragments.
{% extends %} must be the first template tag, and block names are global to the inheritance chain: a duplicate block name silently overrides instead of erroring.

Template lookup is name-based across every loader in TEMPLATES; two apps shipping the same fragment path shadow each other according to loader order, producing surprising output in one deployment and not another.
